key_insight: The paper experimentally shows that continuous-variable QAOA can be run on a quad-rail lattice cluster state, with depth-2 outperforming depth-1 but deeper circuits giving diminishing returns in practice.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a programmable measurement-based quantum computing route for solving quadratic optimization problems, informing how CV hardware and circuit depth trade off against noise and classical optimizer performance.
method: Mapped arbitrary quadratic cost functions onto a quad-rail lattice (QRL) cluster-state architecture.
Prepared a continuous-variable QAOA ansatz on a programmable measurement-based CV platform.
Optimized variational parameters with Bayesian optimization and tested multiple QAOA depths.
evidence_signal: Experiments on multi-variable quadratic optimization problems up to 100 modes showed improved performance from depth 1 to 2, while idealized simulations predicted continued gains with depth.
watch_item: Performance is limited by noise accumulation and classical optimization difficulty, so deeper CV-QAOA circuits may not scale straightforwardly on current hardware.
paper_title: Experimental implementation of continuous-variable QAOA on a quad-rail lattice cluster state
